title: Mushaf or printed al-Hujurat 49:10
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 2: Hadith, akhlaq and Important Lessons
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y8 lesson 11 (Mushaf or printed al-Hujurat 49:10)
intro: Lesson 11: Hadith: the believers are like one body. To understand what the hadith of the one body teaches about how Muslims should care for each other

passage.title: Bukhari and Muslim
paras: The example of the believers in their love, mercy and compassion for one another is that of one body: when one part aches, the whole body responds with sleeplessness and fever.

head: Part
Meaning
rows: Feeling each other's pain and acting

questions.q: Explain what the hadith teaches about Muslim brotherhood.
questions.a: Muslims should love, show mercy and help each other, feeling one another's pain like one body.
questions.model: Point: Muslims are connected like one body. Evidence: 'when one part aches, the whole body responds' (Bukhari and Muslim). Explain: a Muslim should not ignore another's suffering. Link: 49:10 calls the believers brothers.

questions.q: Which ayah says the believers are brothers?
In the portal response box, write a PEEL paragraph: 'How can a Year 8 pupil live by the hadith of the one body?' Start: 'One way a Year 8 pupil can live by this hadith is ...'
questions.a: PEEL paragraph with the hadith quoted and two practical actions
questions.model: Teacher writes the Point and Evidence: 'One way is to make du'a and give for Muslims suffering in a disaster. The Prophet ﷺ said the believers are like one body (Bukhari and Muslim).'

questions.q: how does the hadith apply to how we treat a classmate who is sad?
questions.a: Notice, check on them, help, tell a teacher if needed.

questions.q: does the hadith mean we only care about Muslims?
questions.a: No: Islam teaches mercy to all; this hadith describes the special bond of the believers.

questions.q: Back to our ponder: why one body?
questions.a: Muslims should feel each other's pain and respond with help.
